chunks: It is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام or Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:
A borrowed item is not subject to liability upon its borrower unless that is stipulated, except what is of gold or silver, for indeed those two are guaranteed whether it is stipulated or not.
And he عليه السلام said: If an item is borrowed without its owner’s permission and it perishes, then the borrower is liable.

key_terms.الْعَارِيَّةُ: a loaned or borrowed item given for use without transfer of ownership
key_terms.ذَهَبٍ: gold, which is treated here as an exception in liability
key_terms.ضَمَانٌ: legal liability or financial responsibility for loss or damage
key_terms.فِضَّةٍ: silver, which is also treated here as an exception in liability
key_terms.مَضْمُونَتَانِ: both subject to guarantee or liability
key_terms.مُسْتَعِيرِهَا: the one who borrows and uses the loaned item
key_terms.يُشْتَرَطَ: to be made a condition or stipulated in the agreement

ai.seo_question: Is a borrower liable for a borrowed item in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on borrowed property, stating that the borrower is generally not liable unless liability is stipulated. An exception is made for gold and silver, which remain guaranteed in all cases, and any item taken without the owner’s permission is also the borrower’s liability if it perishes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4083 - It is narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah (as) or (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)), who said:
"A borrowed item (ariyyah) is not guaranteed by the borrower unless it is stipulated, except in the case of gold or silver, as these are guaranteed whether stipulated or not."
Imam (as) also said: "If an item is borrowed without the owner's permission and it perishes, the borrower is liable for it."
